823452.text: PHILADELPHIA – Rookie Phillies' outfielder Gabriel Rincones Jr. hit his first career home run in the second inning. Zack Wheeler tossed six scoreless innings, striking out a season-high nine, to drop his ERA to 2.01. Tim Mayza, Jonathan Bowlan, and Chase Shugart combined to finish out the five-hit shutout. Trea Turner exited in the 8th inning with a right wrist contusion after being hit by a pitch from Marlins' reliever William Kempner.

822724.text: WASHINGTON – The Nationals scored five runs in the fifth inning to pull away. Dylan Crews smacked a three-run homer in the frame off Mason Black. The Royals called on righty Mitch Spence for a spot start after Seth Lugo was played on the 7-day concussion injured list over the weekend, but Spence could only get through four innings. Curtis Mead and Luis Garcia Jr. had 2 RBIs for the Nats. Andrew Alvarez made his third start of the season for Washington, pitching four innings and striking out five.

823451.text: PHILADELPHIA – Kyle Schwarber, making his first start at first base since 2021, hit his league-leading 25th home run of the season in the 4th inning. The Phillies scored seven runs across the first two innings, aided by two-run homers from Brandon Marsh and Alec Bohm. Jesus Luzardo was excellent for seven innings, striking out nine and allowing two runs. Tyler Phillips, who had been a savior for a beleaguered Marlins' rotation, was torched for eight runs in four innings. Esteury Ruiz hit his fourth homer of the year for Miami.

822723.text: WASHINGTON - Curtis Mead hit a go-ahead three-run homer in the seventh to give the Nationals a lead that they would not relinquish. Gus Varland allowed a solo home run in the ninth, but held strong and recorded his sixth save. The Royals have the worst record in the American League.

824750.text: BOSTON – Back up from the minor leagues, Davis Schneider went 2-for-4 with a home run and a double to lead the Blue Jays. George Springer hit his 300th career home run in the ninth inning. Dylan Cease threw 108 pitches in five innings but struck out seven for Toronto. Louie Varland locked down his 13th save of the season, working around a walk and a hit in the ninth. Jarren Duran hit his 12th homer of the year in the 8th inning.

823535.text: NEW YORK – Rookie Spencer Jones hit the first home run of his career at Yankee Stadium in the 2nd inning. The Yankees scored four runs in the third inning and six in the fourth, with Ben Rice and Paul Goldschmidt going deep in the fourth inning. Cody Bellinger and Anthony Volpe both had three hits. Gerrit Cole shut down the White Sox for six innings, striking out six and allowing just three hits. Ryan Yarbrough recorded a three inning save.

824504.text: CINCINNATI – The Reds jumped all over Kodai Senga in his first game back from the injured list, scoring four runs in the first inning. Sal Stewart and Spencer Steer homered in the frame and that was more than enough. Brady Singer and the Cincinnati bullpen held off the Mets. Senga was placed on the injured list with a back strain in late April after struggling badly to a 9.00 ERA through four starts.

824912.text: ATLANTA – The game began on Tuesday but was suspended in the second inning due to rain with the Giants ahead 3-2. When the two teams reconvened on Wednesday afternoon, the Giants got straight to business. Rafael Devers, Jung Hoo Lee, and Willy Adames each homered. Robbie Ray threw 6 1/3 shutout innings with eight strikeouts.

823775.text: MILWAUKEE – Garrett Mitchell launched a go-ahead home run in the seventh inning. Robert Gasser pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings, striking out five. Aaron Ashby recorded his 10th win of the season out of the bullpen, which is most among all pitchers in the majors. The record for most wins by a reliever was set by Roy Face in 1959 with 18.

824913.text: ATLANTA – Luis Arraez and Bryce Eldridge hit back-to-back home runs in the second inning. The Braves made things close in the ninth, bringing the tying run to the plate with one out, but Tristan Beck shut it down to record his first save of the season and finish the twin-bill sweep.

824503.text: CINCINNATI – Nolan McLean held the Reds to one run over seven innings and the Mets resurgent offense did the rest of the work to salvage the series finale. McLean has struggled with his command his last few outings but he was able to walk just one batter and record his first win in June. The Mets jumped all over Nick Lodolo for seven runs allowed in 4 2/3 innings. Juan Soto and Francisco Alvarez each recorded three hits.

822721.text: WASHINGTON – Luinder Avila rebounded from an outing last week where he gave up eight runs and only recorded two outs by tossing 5 2/3 innings of one run ball. Carter Jensen led off the game with a home run. John Rave, Lane Thomas, and Michael Massey also homered. Jensen went 4-for-4 and got on base all five times at the plate.

823450.text: PHILADELPHIA – Kyle Stowers belted a pair of home runs and drove in five runs, while Owen Caissie, Joe Mack and Jakob Marsee also went deep. Phillies’ rookie starter Andrew Painter was demoted to the minors after the game.

824178.text: HOUSTON – Peter Lambert continued his surprising season by tossing seven innings of two hit ball. Lambert is 4-0 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.15 WHIP and .212 opponents’ batting average in his past five starts and has saved the Astros, who have dealt with a mountain of injuries to their rotation. Jeremy Pena swatted his fourth homer of the season. Josh Hader allowed a home run in the ninth, but was able to strike out three and snag his fourth save.

823044.text: ST. LOUIS – Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. powered the Padres to a big win with three hits each as they avoided the sweep. Griffin Canning worked behind an opener and recorded his best outing of the season with 4 1/3 innings of one-run ball.

823940.text: LOS ANGELES – Shohei Ohtani gave up a season-high four runs on the mound and dealt with a blister but the Dodgers were still able to complete the three-game sweep. Freddie Freeman hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the sixth inning.

825072.text: PHOENIX – Corbin Carroll smashed a grand slam in the second inning and Eduardo Rodriguez continued his strong season to get his 100th career win. The eight runs were the most the Diamondbacks had scored in a game since a 9-1 win over the Rockies on May 24. Rodriguez pitched seven strong innings, striking out five and allowing one run. Tommy Troy and Ketel Marte both knocked in two runs and Gabriel Moreno went 3-for-3 with a walk.

824746.text: BOSTON – Scheduled starter Max Scherzer was placed on the IL just hours before first pitch but the Blue Jays’ bullpen was ready on short notice. In the first of 16 games in the next 16 days, Braydon Fisher opened and six relievers followed to shut out the Red Sox. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. went 2-for-4 with two RBIs.

823536.text: NEW YORK – With new NBA champions Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson in attendance, Cody Bellinger finished a triple shy of the cycle. The Yanks have built a 3 1/2-game lead in the AL East, their largest advantage since April 7.

823774.text: MILWAUKEE – Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt, called up yesterday, logged his first MLB hits, run scored, RBI and stolen base for the Brewers. Jackson Chourio homered for the sixth inning in the last seven games. Milwaukee starter Brandon Sproat exited in the fourth inning with a hamstring cramp but Chad Patrick, Aaron Ashby, and Grant Anderson pitched 5 1/3 one-hit innings in relief.

824668.text: CHICAGO – Pete Crow-Armstrong homered for the third straight game. In 15 games in June, Crow-Armstrong is now hitting .406/.435/.906 with 14 extra-base hits, 11 RBIs, 12 runs and four steals. Dansby Swanson swatted his first home run in 86 plate appearances during a seven-run third inning. Sterlin Thompson hit the first two home runs of his career for the Rockies.

824992.text: WEST SACRAMENTO – Ryan O’Hearn set a career-high with six RBIs. Marcell Ozuna belted his first home run in more than a month. All nine Pirates starters recorded a hit.  Zack Gelof extended the longest active hitting streak in the majors to 21 games.

823127.text: SEATTLE – Kyle Bradish pitched into the eighth inning, allowing one run and striking out a career-high 12 as the Orioles evened the series. Gunnar Henderson hit his 15th home run of the season in the third. Blaze Alexander went 3-for-3 with a walk. Orioles’ closer Ryan Helsley was roughed up for two home runs in his first game off the injured list. Mariners' outfielder Julio Rodríguez left the game early with hamstring spasms.

824748.text: BOSTON – Brandon Valenzuela hit a go-ahead RBI double with two outs in the ninth inning to lead the Blue Jays to complete the three-game sweep. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. hit his first home run in over a month and just his fourth of the season as he tries to break out of a season-long power outage. Trey Yesavage pitched 7 1/3 strong innings but left with the game tied. The Red Sox have lost four games in a row and are now 15 1/2 games out of first in the AL East.

824911.text: ATLANTA – The game was postponed due to the rain and will be made up on August 31.

823772.text: MILWAUKEE – Guardians’ rookie Travis Bazzana hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the seventh inning. Kyle Manzardo and David Fry almost hit home runs. Parker Messick delivered six innings of two-run ball and a season-high-tying nine strikeouts.

822889.text: ARLINGTON, Texas – Trevor Larnach, Josh Bell, and Ryan Kreidler all homered as the Twins wrapped up a series sweep. Minnesota outscored the Rangers a combined 9-0 in the first inning across all three games. Larnach went 7-for-11 at the plate in the final two games.

823125.text: SEATTLE – Bryan Woo shined in the series finale twirling seven shutout innings against an Orioles’ lineup that got him for seven runs in five innings in his last start. This was the first time the Orioles were shut out all season. Woo also tied a season high with nine strikeouts and exited to a roaring ovation. The Mariners’ offense got all their offense in the first inning courtesy of a Cole Young RBI double and a Colt Emerson two-run single. The Mariners are clinging to a 1 1/2 game lead in the AL West and head into a weekend series against the last-place Red Sox.

823448.text: PHILADELPHIA – Juan Soto homered twice and Sean Manaea continued to pitch well in his return to the rotation as the Mets took the first of three in Philadelphia. Eric Wagaman hit a go-ahead single in a three-run seventh inning.

823124.text: SEATTLE – Ranger Suarez no-hit the Mariners for 6 1/3 innings until Josh Naylor broke up the bid with a double in the seventh inning. Suarez struck out five and lowered his ERA to 2.93. Caleb Durbin went 3-for-4 at the plate and hit his fifth homer of the year. Marcelo Mayer had two hits and drove in three runs. Julio Rodriguez homered in the ninth for Seattle. The Red Sox ended a four-game losing streak. The Mariners hold a narrow 1/2 game lead in the AL West.

823936.text: LOS ANGELES – The Dodgers walked it off against Orioles’ closer Ryan Helsley in the ninth on a wild play. Dalton Rushing lined a single to right to tie the game at five but right fielder Tyler O’Neill’s throw home bounced away from the catcher, allowing Ryan Ward to score. Gunnar Henderson and Pete Alonso hit back-to-back home runs in the sixth inning to tie the game.

825069.text: PHOENIX – Corbin Carroll tied the D'backs’ franchise record for career triples with 52 and drove in four runs. Starter Michael Soroka left the game in the second inning with an injury. Victor Caratini and Royce Lewis went deep.

824990.text: WEST SACRAMENTO – The Athletics came back from a seven-run deficit in the sixth inning, capped off by a Nick Kurtz walk-off walk in the 10th. The A’s have  an AL-best 21 comeback wins.

824345.text: DENVER – On a night where Kyle Freeland became the second Rockie in franchise history to eclipse 1,000 strikeouts and pitched into the eighth inning in his best start of the year, Colorado’s bats had their starter’s back. Braxton Fulford lined a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth. T.J. Rumfield hit his 11th home run of the season.

824097.text: KANSAS CITY – With All-star shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. on the bench after exiting the previous night’s game with a knee injury, the Royals were still able to pull out a gutsy win. Seth Lugo came off the concussion IL to throw six innings. The Cardinals made it close in the ninth, scoring three runs and bringing the go-ahead run to the plate, but Alex Lange got a groundout to secure his fifth save.

824179.text: HOUSTON – Tatsuya Imai rebounded from a blowup start last week against the Royals by striking out a career-high 11 in six innings. Jose Altuve homered and drove in four runs and Jeremy Pena had three hits and three RBIs. The Astros pulled away against the Cleveland bullpen by scoring seven runs in the final three innings. Rhys Hoskins homered for Cleveland.

822886.text: ARLINGTON, Texas – The two teams combined to score 11 runs in a crazy first inning but Texas pulled away late in the game to end a three game losing streak. Wyatt Langford had three hits, including a home run. Jacob Latz picked up his 13th save. Ty France hit two home runs, including a grand slam in the first, and drove in five in a losing effort.

824910.text: ATLANTA – 35-year-old Martin Perez outdueled rookie star Jacob Misiorowski across six innings. Mauricio Dubon put the Braves ahead in the sixth with a go-ahead two-out single. Mike Yastrzemski added on a big insurance solo home run in the seventh. Eli White threw out Jackson Chourio at the plate to prevent the game-tying run from scoring in the ninth inning. Raisel Iglesias gave up a run, but recorded his 15th save.

822966.text: TAMPA BAY – Jonathan Aranda hit a three-run home run off the foul pole in the third inning after the Nationals jumped out to an early 2-0 lead. Jonny DeLuca, just activated from the injured list after missing nearly a month, added on a solo home run in the eighth. Bryan Baker locked down his 19th save of the season. Luis Garcia Jr. hit his tenth home run and C.J. Abrams hit his 15th. The Rays won for just the eighth time in their last 23 games.

823534.text: NEW YORK – Cam Schlittler struck out 13 across six dominant shutout innings to lower his season ERA to 1.71 and become the youngest pitcher in Yankees’ history to strike out 13+ batters and walk none in a game. Schlittler threw 66 of his 96 pitches for strikes. Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Ben Rice homered in the fourth inning to provide the offense. Rice ranks second in MLB with a .616 slugging percentage and 1.005 OPS. The Yankee bullpen pitched three hitless innings.

824264.text: DETROIT – Back-to-back Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal struck out eight in his first start back at Comerica Park after missing the last six weeks due to elbow surgery. Kerry Carpenter hit a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth to give the Tigers the lead for good. Junior Perez recorded his first big league hit and later on hit his first career home run for the White Sox off the All-Star Skubal.

824663.text: CHICAGO – The Cubs jumped all over Kevin Gausman for seven runs in the first inning, including a Carson Kelly grand slam. Ben Brown, who has been fantastic since being moved to the rotation in early May,  went six innings of two run ball.

823853.text: MIAMI – Owen Caissie went 3-for-3, drove in three runs, and finished a triple shy of the cycle to lead the Marlins. Caissie also hit a go-ahead sac fly in the seventh inning. Pete Fairbanks picked up his 10th save.

823854.text: MIAMI – Max Meyer allowed two runs in five innings to win his eighth consecutive decision to start the season, Heriberto Hernández homered and the Marlins won their seventh straight game at home. Jakob Marsee doubled and singled for the Marlins, who are 13-4 in June. Otto López became the first player to reach 100 hits in the majors this season.

824263.text: DETROIT – Troy Melton allowed one hit in six innings and the Tigers’ offense came alive late as Detroit won its second straight game after losing four of five. The Tigers took the lead in the sixth when Spencer Torkelson doubled and scored on James Outman’s single. Jake Rogers made it 3-1 later in the inning with an RBI single. Chicago didn’t get its second hit until Braden Montgomery doubled off Tyler Holton with one out in the seventh.

823532.text: NEW YORK – Sal Stewart tied a career high with six RBIs and the Reds pulled away for a rout of the Yankees. The rookie gave the Reds the lead with a two-run double in the third off Will Warren and lifted a sacrifice fly during a four-run fifth. Stewart capped his day with a bases-clearing double in the eighth that expanded the lead to 9-1. Spencer Steer hit a three-run homer in the fifth as the Reds won for the sixth time in 17 games. Rookie Edwin Arroyo had four hits and reached base five times as the Reds finished with 15 hits.

824665.text: CHICAGO – Kazuma Okamoto hit a three-run home run to cap a five-run eighth inning and the Blue Jays rallied from a five-run deficit. Daulton Varsho returned from the 10-day injured list and added a three-run shot as Toronto won for the fourth time in five games. Louis Varland got the final six outs for his 15th save.

822885.text: ARLINGTON, Texas – Manny Machado hit a three-run homer in the 10th inning and tied his season high of five RBIs. Jackson Merrill hit a game-tying single in the eighth. Mason Miller earned his 20th save despite giving up a run. Miller struck out two as the Rangers fanned a season-high 17 times.

822967.text: TAMPA BAY – Dylan Crews homered in the ninth inning and C.J. Abrams went deep for a second consecutive game. The Nationals look to win a franchise record-tying sixth consecutive road series on Sunday. Clayton Beeter finished for his fifth save, striking out Ben Williamson with the tying run on second base to end it.

824909.text: ATLANTA – Ozzie Albies hit two homers, including a walk-off, two-run blast in the ninth inning to give the Braves a come-from-behind win. After Matt Olson singled off Aaron Ashby with one out, Albies delivered the decisive shot over the right field wall. Chris Sale gave up five hits and two unearned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Joey Bart became the Braves’ franchise-record eighth catcher to appear in a game this season.

824180.text: HOUSTON – Rookie Travis Bazzana set career highs with four hits, two homers, five RBIs and three runs scored. Kyle Manzardo hit a two-run homer in the third inning to break a 1-1 tie, and tacked on an RBI single in the seventh. Patrick Bailey added three hits and two runs scored. Joey Cantillo pitched a career-high tying eight innings and matched a season high with nine strikeouts.

823447.text: PHILADELPHIA – Kyle Schwarber homered three times, including twice in Philadelphia’s eight-run third inning, and Bryce Harper hit for the cycle as the  Phillies routed the Mets. It was the fifth career three-homer game for Schwarber, who was 4-for-5 with six RBIs. Harper hit a solo home run in the first inning,  doubled and singled in the third, then hit a two-run triple in the fifth for his first career cycle.

824342.text: DENVER – Jake McCarthy hit a leadoff inside-the-park home run off Paul Skenes and the Rockies survived another tense ninth inning. The Pirates, as they did Friday night, had the tying run on third with less that two outs in the ninth. Jaden Hill came on and hit Nick Gonzalez to load the bases before striking out Tyler Callihan. Jake Mangum then hit a grounder to third baseman Kyle Karros, and the game ended when umpires determined Karros was interfered with by Billy Cook.

824988.text: WEST SACRAMENTO – Walbert Ureña and three relievers combined on a five-hitter as the Angels bounced back from blowing a seven-run lead in the series opener. Denzer Guzman hit his second home run of the season, Zach Neto and Nolan Schanuel each drove in two runs. Jo Adell and Donovan Walton each had three hits.

823937.text: LOS ANGELES – Trevor Rogers allowed one hit over a dominating seven scoreless innings. Blaze Alexander had a two-run double for the Orioles. The Dodgers nearly rallied for the second consecutive night. Tommy Edman hit what appeared to be a line drive to right for the final out. But Leody Taveras dropped the ball allowing Freddie Freeman to score before Kyle Tucker struck out against Yennier Cano, who earned his first save.

823126.text: SEATTLE – Wilyer Abreu hit a two-run homer and Connelly Early gave up two hits and a run in six innings. Early gave up two hits and a run in the first inning, but didn’t allow another hit through the rest of his six inning. The Red Sox stole three bases in the game, with Caleb Durbin swiping two.

825068.text: PHOENIX – Byron Buxton hit a grand slam in a 10-run fifth inning. The Twins had 16 hits in the fourth and fifth innings when they sent a combined 24 batters to the plate. Taj Bradley went five innings, giving up three hits and two runs. The Twins have won five of their last six games.

823286.text: SAN DIEGO – Manny Machado sent a pitch from Raisel Iglesias into center field to give the Padres their sixth walk-off victory of the season. San Diego rallied from an early 4-0 deficit.

823210.text: SAN FRANCISCO – Robbie Ray held the Athletics to an unearned run and two hits in eight innings. Ray struck out six and walked four. In his previous outing, the left-hander allowed two hits in 6 1/3 shutout innings. Caleb Kilian worked a scoreless ninth in this one for his fifth save. Zack Gelof was forced to leave the game with a laceration and contusion after getting spiked while making a tag, and his hitting streak ended at 24 games.

824017.text: LOS ANGELES – In his third career start, rookie right-hander Ryan Johnson gave up one hit over six scoreless innings, Nolan Schanuel hit a two-run home run and the Angels ended a three-game losing streak. Johnson carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning before Jeremiah Jackson hit one-out a line drive single to center field. Johnson allowed one walk with career highs of eight strikeouts and six innings, while throwing 90 pitches.

824340.text: DENVER – Wilyer Abreu and Nate Eaton drove in two runs each to back an 11-strikeout performance from Sonny Gray, who improved to an AL-best 9-1. Gray allowed a run on six hits with three walks in seven innings. The right-hander’s 11 strikeouts were a season high. Boston improved to 20-20 on the road one day after blowing their first ninth inning lead this season. Eaton went 3-for-4.. Willi Castro and Ezequiel Tovar both hit their sixth home runs for Colorado.

823690.text: MINNESOTA – Freddie Freeman and Andy Pages each had three of the Dodgers’ season high-tying 17 hits and Justin Wrobleski worked seven innings while retiring 14 of the final 16 hitters he faced. Mookie Betts, Alex Freeland, Alex Call and Chuckie Robinson had two hits apiece. The outcome could have been worse, but the Dodgers finished 5 for 19 with runners in scoring position and left 13 on base.

823043.text: ST. LOUIS – Nolan Arenado and Lourdes Gurriel Jr. had run-scoring hits in the ninth. All the runs in the game were scored in the ninth inning. The Cardinals nearly came back in the bottom of the inning but JJ Wetherholt struck out swinging against Brandyn Garcia to end the game.

822963.text: TAMPA BAY – Tampa Bay native Jac Caglianone continued his hot June by homering twice and driving in three runs in the Royals’ victory over the reeling Rays. Caglianone's had his third multihomer game this month. His nine homers in June are tied with Nick Kurtz most in the AL.

823614.text: NEW YORK – Pete Crow-Armstrong hit a three-run homer and Dansby Swanson also went deep and drove in four. Cubs' starter Edward Cabrera hurt his left leg stretching to catch a throw at first base in the fifth inning and was carted off the field. Francisco Alvarez homered and knocked in three for the last-place Mets.

822799.text: TORONTO – Former Blue Jay Joey Loperfido hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the 11th inning.

823365.text: PITTSBURGH – Cole Young hit a two-run home run in the seventh inning in his first major league game in his hometown. Young grew up in Pittsburgh’s northern suburbs and starred at North Allegheny High School.  Andrés Muñoz pitched a perfect ninth for his 14th save.

823849.text: MIAMI – Sandy Alcantara set the Marlins' franchise career record for strikeouts and won his fifth consecutive start in June. With a strikeout of Kyle Higashioka in the seventh inning, Alcantara surpassed Ricky Nolasco for the most strikeouts in club history with 1,002. Heriberto Hernández homered and doubled, while Joe Mack and Owen Caissie also went deep for the Marlins.

824262.text: DETROIT – Jazz Chisholm Jr. hit a go-ahead two run homer and scored twice as New York ended a three-game losing streak and stopped Detroit’s four-game winning streak. Carlos Rodón picked up the win, allowing three runs and six hits with two walks in 5 1/3 innings. Three relievers finished, with David Bednar getting the final four outs for his 15th save.

822718.text: WASHINGTON – Bryson Stott’s three-run homer highlighted Philadelphia’s eight-run outburst in the ninth inning and the Phillies rallied to beat the Nationals. Jesus Luzardo struck out 13.

824501.text: CINCINNATI – Brandon Sproat pitched one-hit ball for six shutout innings and had a career-high 10 strikeouts. Jake Bauers and Andrew Vaughn drove in runs for the Brewers, who have won 12 of their last 13 series at Great American Ballpark. The Brewers spoiled the return of Reds' shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who went 0 for 3 and struck out twice in his first game since May 31

824584.text: CHICAGO – Miguel Vargas hit a go-ahead home run in the sixth inning, Sean Burke struck out six in 6 1/3 innings, and the Chicago White Sox claimed sole possession of first place in the AL Central. Sean Newcomb pitched the final 2 2/3 innings for his second save. The White Sox are 22-4 in their last 26 home games, 11-1 against the AL Central at home and have won nine straight home series. Guardians rookie Kahlil Watson hit his first career home run in the fifth inning.

823850.text: MIAMI – Otto López homered to raise his major league-leading batting average to .340. Xavier Edwards had an RBI single in the fifth. Lopez’s two-run shot in the eighth off reliever Cole Winn gave him a 33rd multi-hit game. The Marlins improved to a major league-best 16-5 in June. Miami is 42-39 at the halfway point and has won five consecutive home series. Pete Fairbanks gave up a run, but was able to secure his 12th save.

823613.text: NEW YORK – Dansby Swanson hit a tiebreaking three-run homer in the sixth inning and added a grand slam in the eighth inning Wednesday, lifting the Cubs over the reeling New York Mets in the opener of a day-night doubleheader. Dozens of Norwegian soccer fans adorned in soccer garb in center field chanted and danced a conga line throughout the game.

823611.text: NEW YORK – Dansby Swanson had a go-ahead RBI triple and four RBIs to cap a monster doubleheader. The Mets fell a season-high 12 games under .500

824583.text: CHICAGO – Khalil Watson singled in the go-ahead run in the 10th inning for his third RBI of the day, and the Guardians survived a ninth-inning collapse to tie the White Sox for the AL Central lead.

824341.text: DENVER – Tyler Freeman’s safety squeeze bunt in the eighth inning drove in the go-ahead run and the Rockies took two out of three from the last-place Red Sox. Cole Carrigg drove in three runs. Freeman put down a bunt against Justin Slaten along the first-base line that scored Mickey Moniak to put the Rockies up. Jimmy Herget grabbed his second save.

824018.text: ANAHEIM – Logan O'Hoppe's check-swing trickler scored Nolan Schanuel from third base in the tenth inning. Wade Meckler tied the game with a two-run single in the eighth.

823367.text: PITTSBURGH – Braxton Ashcraft pitched six strong innings, batterymate Endy Roriguez drove in three runs and Ryan O’Hearn had four hits and three RBIs. Ashcraft became the first Pirates pitcher to have at least two starts in the same season with at least 10 strikeouts and zero walks since at least 1901. Bryan Woo started with three hitless innings, but then fell apart in the fourth. He gave up five runs and six hits. Spencer Horwitz left the game with hamstring discomfort in the fourth.

822965.text: TAMPA BAY – Griffin Jax pitched five strong innings, Yandy Díaz tied B.J. Upton’s franchise mark of 447 career RBIs with a fourth inning single. Jax struck out seven while allowing two unearned runs and five hits. It was his fourth start in a row with at least five innings pitched and less than two earned runs allowed. Bryan Baker gave up a run in the ninth, but closed it out for his 20th save.

824259.text: DETROIT – Paul Goldschmidt hit two home runs, including a leadoff home run, and Jasson Domínguez hit a go-ahead, two-run shot in the sixth inning off Tarik Skubal. Detroit's starter tied a career high by giving up three home runs, allowing that many in a game for the first time since 2021. The two-time reigning Cy Young Award winner gave up only one other hit, didn’t walk a batter and had nine strikeouts over six innings.

822719.text: WASHINGTON – Derek Hill hit a two-out, two-run pinch home run in the ninth inning one day after the Phillies scored eight runs in the ninth to come back from a deficit against the Nationals. Curtis Mead, Luis Garcia Jr., and Jorbit Vivas all homered for Washington.

822798.text: TORONTO – Joey Loperfido scored the tiebreaking run on Jeff Hoffman’s errant pickoff throw in the eighth inning. Loperfido tripled off the center field wall with one out and scored when Hoffman’s pickoff throw sailed past third baseman Kazuma Okamoto. Okamoto was standing well wide of the base. Josh Hader nabbed his sixth save. Luis Urias got doubled off second base after Cam Smith made a leaping catch at the wall in the eighth.

824500.text: CINCINNATI – William Contreras and Jake Bauers hit back-to-back homers in the third inning and the Brewers completed a three-game sweep. The Reds loaded the bases with one out in the ninth against Joel Kuhnel, but Dane Myers ground into a double play.

823691.text: MINNEAPOLIS – Mookie Betts backed Shohei Ohtani with his 300th career home run, three hits and slick defense as the Dodgers finished a three-game sweep. Ohtani finished six innings with five hits and three walks allowed and eight strikeouts. Max Muncy and Alex Call drove in the tying and go-ahead runs and Tanner Scott secured his 11th save. Ohtani and catcher Dalton Rushing appeared to argue on the mound in the second inning

823041.text: ST. LOUIS – LuJames Groover and Ketel Marte hit back-to-back home runs to cap a six-run fourth inning. Groover's was the first of his career. Mitch Bratt allowed one run and two hits and two walks in three innings as he became the first Canadian pitcher to make his major league debut with the Diamondbacks. Every hitter in the D'backs' lineup had at least one hit.

823284.text: SAN DIEGO – Ty France homered and JP Sears won his season debut to complete a three-game sweep of the Atlanta Braves. Sears allowed two runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings, struck out five and walked two. He was recalled from Triple-A El Paso on Tuesday after right-hander Lucas Giolito went on the injured list.

823208.text: SAN FRANCISCO – Rafael Devers hit a tying home run leading off the ninth and Victor Bericoto launched a walk-off home run. Max Muncy homered with two outs in the eighth to break up a scoreless game. Jacob Wilson broke up Tyler Mahle's no-hit bid in the fifth inning with a single.

824255.text: DETROIT – Keider Montero pitched seven scoreless innings and a big fourth inning helped the Tigers snap a three-game losing streak. James Outman belted a three-run homer and Colt Keith and Kerry Carpenter added on solo shots of their own.

823206.text: SAN FRANCISCO – Mauricio Dubon and Matt Olson had two hits and Ozzie Albies drove in two runs as the Braves bounced back from a sweep at the hands of the Padres as they continue their west coast trip. Atlanta has won just four of their 14 games. Reynaldo Lopez and Hurston Waldrep pitched well as they both audition for a starting role in a Braves' rotation that has been decimated with injuries.

824821.text: BALTIMORE – Luis Garcia Jr. went deep twice and drove in five runs to help the Nationals get back above .500. Garcia Jr. went 7-for-11 (.636) with three homers in the series to continue a scorching June. He’s second in the NL with 11 home runs this month. Pete Alonso hit a two-run homer for the O’s in the first inning, his 19th of the season.

823362.text: PITTSBURGH – Ryan O’Hearn went deep twice and drove in four for Pittsburgh. O’Hearn answered the Reds’ comeback from a 4-0 deficit with a tie-breaking home run in the fifth to put the Pirates back up 5-4 and then added insurance with a three-run shot in the eighth to make it 8-4.

822795.text: TORONTO – Jarred Kelenic scored from second base on a wild pitch with two outs in the ninth inning to edge the Rangers past the slumping Blue Jays. Louis Varland’s pitch bounced away from Alejandro Kirk and the pinch-runner Kelenic scampered around to score the go-ahead run. Nathan Lukes tied it in the eighth with a two-run shot off Cole Winn. Joc Pederson's leadoff homer on the first pitch of the game was his fourth homer in five games.

824256.text: DETROIT – Houston overcame a three-run deficit to tie the game in the eighth and the four-run tenth was capped off by a Christian Walker three-run homer. Raynel Delgado belted his first-career home run in the seventh.

824422.text: CLEVELAND – Rhys Hoskins delivered a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth to push the Guardians get past the Mariners. Chase DeLauter had the game-tying hit earlier in the frame. The Mariners dropped to below .500 and to second place in the AL West for the first time in over a month.

822959.text: ST. PETERSBURG – For the fourth straight game and for the sixth time in four games, Junior Caminero went deep as the Rays extended their winning streak to five games. Caminero’s 463-foot bomb in the fifth inning was the longest of his career. Drew Rasmussen pitched six shutout innings and lowered his ERA to 2.45, second in the AL. Cedric Mullins added on another home run for the Rays. Ketel Marte homered for Arizona.

823608.text: QUEENS – Kyle Schwarber’s MLB-leading 30th home run of the season was also a go-ahead two-run shot that put the Phillies ahead for good as they managed the series finale. Despite walking eight, Phillies pitching did enough to wrap up another series win. A.J. Ewing hit a game-tying two-run homer in the sixth inning for the Mets who continue to slide, even under new manager Andy Green.

823686.text: MINNEAPOLIS – Ryan Kreidler’s go-ahead solo home run off Seth Halvorsen in the seventh gave the Twins a lead that they would not relinquish. Connor Prielipp struck out ten across six innings in the best start of his young career. Yoendrys Gómez needed just four pitches to get three outs in the ninth as he recorded his eighth save.

824580.text: CHICAGO – Carter Jensen extended his hitting streak to 19 games going 3-for-5 with two RBIs and delivered the deciding run-scoring double in the fourth inning as the Royals salvaged a game from the White Sox. The Royals’ bullpen allowed just one hit over the final five innings. Alex Lange pitched a perfect ninth to collect his seventh save in seven opportunities.

823769.text: MILWAUKEE – The Cubs scored three times in the tenth and Jordan Wicks worked out of a bases-loaded, no out jam in the bottom half of the inning.

823037.text: ST. LOUIS – Bryan Torres drove in all the runs for the Cardinals as they salvaged the final game of the series and ended a four-game losing streak. Torres’ second inning two-run blast was all required to get the Redbirds past the scalding hot Marlins. Kyle Leahy was solid in five innings, only allowing a Graham Pauley RBI single in the fifth. The Cardinals struck out just twice all day. Riley O’Brien locked down his 20th save of the season.

824011.text: ANAHEIM – Josh Lowe, who was just recalled from Triple-A, blasted his first career grand slam as the Angels wrapped up a series win. Lowe was called up on Wednesday after spending a month in the minors. Facing veteran Aaron Civale in the second inning, Lowe took the right-hander deep to right field for his sixth homer of the season. Sam Aldegheri struck out four and gave up one run over five innings in his best start of the season. Samy Natera Jr. earned his first big league save with a scoreless ninth inning.

823204.text: SAN FRANCISCO – Robbie Ray and Chris Sale did not disappoint in a pitching duel of former Cy Young award winners. Sale struck out ten in six innings, allowing two runs (one earned) while Ray went eight innings and allowed one unearned run. The Giants scored two runs in the sixth thanks to two Braves’ throwing errors. Caleb Kilian allowed a run in the ninth but locked down his sixth save. Willy Adames exited with back spasms.

823281.text: SAN DIEGO – Mookie Betts drove in two and Emmet Sheehan pitched five sharp innings as the Dodgers took two of three in the series. Shohei Ohtani drove in the first run of the game and Freddie Freeman drew a go-ahead bases-loaded walk in the fifth. Manny Machado’s 15th homer of the season was the only run for San Diego

824744.text: BOSTON – Sonny Gray reached 2,000 career strikeouts and didn’t allow a hit for 7 1/3 innings until Amed Rosario singled to break up the no-hitter in the eighth. The Boston bullpen blew a 2-0 lead late due to some fielding mistakes but Jarren Duran walked off the Yankees with a single in the tenth to complete the four game sweep.

824336.text: DENVER – Jake McCarthy homered on the first pitch of the first inning and launched a grand slam in the fifth on way to a career-high six runs driven in. Every player in the Rockies' lineup had at least one hit. Six players had at least two hits. Ryan Feltner struck out nine and Gabriel Hughes earned the save in his major league debut.

824659.text: CHICAGO – The Cardinals scored a season-high 17 as they clobbered their division rival on a humid afternoon. Alec Burleson and Masyn Winn both drove in four runs. Every player in the Cards' starting lineup reached base. Winn, Nathan Church, and Bryan Torres all went deep. St. Louis has scored 28 runs over the past two days.

822714.text: WASHINGTON – Luis Garcia Jr. continued his scalding June into July with a two-homer game and Daylen Lile also homered twice while driving in four. Garcia Jr., last week's NL Player of the Week, has 8 home runs and 16 RBIs over his last ten games. Rookie Esmerlyn Valdez had three hits and is hitting .552 over his last eight games for Pittsburgh. The Pirates haven't been more than one game above or below .500 since June 7.

823527.text: BRONX – Bracing against sweltering humidity, the Yankees snapped their seven-game losing streak with a win over the visiting Twins. Trent Grisham, activated off the injured list earlier in the day, led off the first inning with a home run. Gerrit Cole was sharp, striking out seven in five innings, and only left the game after a 53 minute rain delay. The Yankee bullpen pitched four shutout innings with David Bednar locking down his 17th save. Ben Rice also homered for New York.

824498.text: CINCINNATI – Samuel Basallo belted an opposite-field two-run homer and batterymate Trevor Rogers pitched five scoreless innings while allowing just two hits. The Orioles scored their first run when Gunnar Henderson swiped third and Tyler Stephenson's throw sailed into left field. That was all they needed as Rogers gave up two hits the rest of the way despite walking a season-high five. Basallo's 13th home run of the year came in the third inning. The Orioles' bullpen allowed three baserunners over the final four innings.

824417.text: CLEVELAND – Steven Kwan's RBI single tied it in the seventh and Kahlil Watson capped off the comeback with a walk-off single into center field past a drawn-in infield. The Guardians have won three in a row while the White Sox have dropped three in a row.

824904.text: ATLANTA – The NL-East leading Braves scored all of their runs off home runs in a four-homer barrage. Matt Olson homered twice while Michael Harris II and Ozzie Albies added on solo blasts. Atlanta recorded just five hits, but four of them were home runs. Raisel Iglesias allowed a run in the ninth and the Mets brought the potential go-ahead run to the plate, but Francisco Lindor grounded out to second to end the game. Juan Soto homered for the Mets.

824173.text: HOUSTON – Junior Caminero's tenth home run in his last ten games was a go-ahead blast off of Steven Okert in the seventh inning as the Rays won their ninth straight game. Nick Martinez allowed three hits in 5 1/3 innings and the Rays' bullpen fired 3 2/3 perfect innings. Nick Fortes homered and drove in a clutch insurance run with an RBI double in the eighth. Yordan Alvarez hit his AL-leading 27th home run for the Astros. Bryan Baker pitched a perfect ninth to pick up his 23rd save.

824013.text: ANAHEIM – Rookie left-hander Jake Bennett pitched the best game of his young career, going 7 2/3 innings, allowing five hits and two runs while striking out six and walking none. Romy Gonzalez had three hits and drove in two. The Angels nearly mounted a comeback in the ninth, bringing the tying run to the plate, but Aroldis Chapman got Jo Adell to bounce into a game-ending double-play. Bennett lost the shutout when Jose Siri homered in the eighth.

824982.text: WEST SACRAMENTO – A six-run first inning, highlighted by a Heriberto Hernandez three-run homer, helped the Marlins cruise to a big victory. Kyle Stowers went 4-for-5 while homering twice. Jacob Marsee and Owen Caissie also went deep for Miami, who is 21-8 since the start of June.

825062.text: PHOENIX – Jackson Chourio's infield-single plus a throwing error brought in two runs, including the go-ahead, for the Brewers. Milwaukee's bullpen saved the day after starter Kyle Harrison departed in the third inning.

823933.text: LOS ANGELES – Teoscar Hernandez hit a seventh inning go-ahead grand slam deep into the left-center field bleachers off Adrian Morejon as the slumping Padres dropped their seventh in a row. Shohei Ohtani tied a season-high by surrendering seven hits and exited with a right biceps issue. L.A. had just two hits heading into the seventh. Tanner Scott struck out the side in the ninth to earn his 12th save.

823120.text: SEATTLE – In a rematch of last year's ALCS, Dylan Cease was sensational for seven scoreless innings and a two-run third inning was all Toronto needed. The 2025 ALCS MVP Vladimir Guerrero Jr. drove in a run with a single in the third. In front of a crowd with plenty of royal blue in it, the AL-strikeout leader Cease put on a show as he K'd nine and allowed just three hits. Andres Gimenez drove in the game's first run with an RBI double. Louis Varland remained perfect in saved chances this season as he earned his 18th. Seattle snapped a three-game win streak.
